newsitem.title: CHINA: China police clear, sweep, wash Tiananmen Square.
newsitem.headline: China police clear, sweep, wash Tiananmen Square.

text.p: Unarmed Chinese police backed by paramilitary personnel cleared Beijing's Tiananmen Square of tens of thousands of sightseers on Monday in preparations for a ceremony to mark Hong Kong's handover to China.
Hundreds of police, with People's Armed Police behind them, advanced in tight-knit ranks on the crowd, pushing reluctant and curious onlookers to the sides of the vast square.

Behind the police walked dozens of sanitary workers, who swept the square of debris left by hundreds of thousands of city residents and tourists from all over China who have flocked to the square in recent days to see the decorations for the handover celebration.

Officials had announced in advance that the clearing of the square would take place shortly after 3.00 p.m. (0700 GMT) and advised Beijing's 11 million residents who were not among the 100,000 invited guests to stay at home and watch television.

Some tried to ignore the police, including groups of card players who moved slowly back in front of the advancing police lines, hoping to finish a last hand before the final touches are made for ceremonies for Hong Kong's handover at midnight.
One woman rolled up paper China and Hong Kong flags in her hand as police pushed her gently but firmly off the square.

"We were hoping to stay for the show, but I guess we'll have to watch it from somewhere else," said the woman, who had travelled from eastern Shandong province for a glimpse in Beijing of an end to 156 years of British colonial rule over Hong Kong, a transfer viewed by Chinese as the end of more than a century and a half of national humiliation.
Dozens of garbage trucks and street washing tankers moved on to the square to join the cleaning operation, gathering up hundreds of bottles, popsicle sticks and discarded flags and scraps of paper.

More than 100,000 people have been invited to join the official party in the square to watch the countdown clock tick away the final thousands of seconds to the moment of handover at midnight on Monday.
China has rarely allowed large crowds to gather on Tiananmen Square since the army crushed student-led pro-democracy demonstrations centred in the square on June 3-4, 1989, killing hundreds.

On Saturday and Sunday nights, hundreds of thousands of people flocked to the square to take photographs of the huge red lanterns as well as thousands of flowers and potted plants and signs welcoming the return of Hong Kong to the motherland.
High above China's capital, a blimp proclaims the impending recovery of the territory, bearing the message "Celebrate the Return of Hong Kong".

Down below, Chinese flags flutter across the city while banners stream across pedestrian bridges and on street corners, shouting: "Wash away 100 years of national shame" and "A better tomorrow for Hong Kong".
The square is due to reopen to the public on Tuesday morning after the ceremonies end with the dawn raising in the square of China's national flag.
